kind.content: Forty-eight letters since 2024 on writing, reading, tools and the odd personal detour. Pick one with a coffee.
Why I write by hand first
Paper is slow, and slow is the point. On first drafts that are allowed to be bad.
The case for fewer, better notes
I kept everything for ten years and found nothing. What changed when I started throwing notes away.
Reading slowly in a fast year
Twelve books, one pencil and a rule: nothing new until the last one has a page of notes.
The white space around a page is where readers talk back. A short history of writing in books.
A drawer of drafts to people who will never read them, and what they taught me about saying things plainly.
Punctuation is timing. A copy editor's confession.
Every book I read twice this year, and which ones got better.
The opening you wrote to find your way in is rarely the one a reader needs.
